public_rationale: The hackathon study, published December 2, 2025, reports functional demonstrations and uneven code quality among novice and mixed-experience teams. Its event is dated only to 2025, and it includes no production-hardening follow-up [e1]. The other study used March–April 2025 videos and describes debugging that combines AI assistance with manual work [e2]. Neither establishes how commonly amateurs encountered material defects or successfully hardened prototypes during November 1–29, 2025, leaving the prevalence claims unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: Neither study provides representative success rates for amateurs hardening prototypes.
The hackathon mixes experience levels and measures demonstrations rather than sustained dependability.
The studies do not jointly measure correctness, security and operational reliability after sustained development.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Amateurs can build prototypes with AI coding, but the generated code tends to be shaky and few can make it robust.

statement.excerpt: (Amateurs can in fact now build prototypes, but the auto-generated code tends to be shaky and few amateurs can make those prototypes robust.)
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: Amateurs can in fact now build prototypes
the auto-generated code tends to be shaky
few amateurs can make those prototypes robust
our_interpretation: Amateurs means people without professional software-development expertise, including non-programmers and beginners.
A prototype demonstrates intended functionality. Robust means sufficiently correct, secure and dependable for its intended real use, including foreseeable errors and edge cases.
Tends to be shaky means quality problems are common, rather than merely possible. Few means successful hardening is uncommon among amateurs attempting it; no exact percentage is imposed.
Use November 1–29, 2025, the latest month-to-publication window for the ongoing observation. Include developments through publication rather than stopping in September.
Earlier studies and later publications can inform the assessment, but only observations tied to the target period can decide its contemporary prevalence claims.
criteria.support_condition: Studies show amateurs producing functional prototypes, commonly encountering material generated-code defects, and only a small share successfully making those prototypes dependable for their intended use.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show amateurs routinely producing dependable applications or successfully hardening prototypes, with material generated-code problems uncommon.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative study tied to November 1–29, 2025, identifying participants’ expertise and tool versions, independently testing prototype defects, and reporting how often amateurs achieved intended-use correctness, security and reliability after a reasonable opportunity to harden their applications.
